core_obligations: Part (1): catenarity is local on X by Topology, Lemma topology-lemma-catenary, so reduce to X = Spec(A) with A a finite type k-algebra and then reduce further to k[x_1, ..., x_n] (proof lines 3854-3864).
Part (2) and part (10): choose an affine neighbourhood U = Spec(A) of x and use dim_x(X) = dim_x(U) to reduce to the affine statement (proof lines 3867-3870 and 3937-3940).

Part (3) and part (4): compare two nonempty affine opens by picking a closed point x of X inside their intersection, which exists by the Jacobson property, and then read off equal dimensions from the affine case; extend a given chain of irreducible closed subsets after meeting an affine open (proof lines 3873-3891).

Part (5): use the bijection Z to Z cap U between irreducible components through x of X and of an affine neighbourhood U, together with dim(Z cap U) = dim(Z), to reduce to the affine max-min formula (proof lines 3894-3902).

Parts (6), (7), (8): reduce the transcendence degree statements to the affine case; part (7) is obtained by observing that Z = closure of {x} contains Z' = closure of {x'} as the start of a maximal chain in Z, so dim(Z) = dim(Z') + 1 (proof lines 3905-3925).

Part (9): part (a) because any open containing x' contains x, part (b) by extending a chain of primes in O_{X,x} by the maximal ideal of O_{X,x'}, parts (c) and (d) formally from part (7) (proof lines 3928-3934).
Part (11): in the equidimensional case dim_x(X) = dim(X) = dim_{x'}(X), so the assertion follows from part (7) (proof lines 3943-3949).
proof_roadmap: Reduce each of the eleven parts to the affine case Spec(A) with A a finite type k-algebra (proof lines 3847-3851).
Route parts (1), (2), (5) and (10) to the corresponding statements on finite type k-algebras (proof lines 3854-3870, 3894-3902, 3937-3940).

Handle the parts that need one extra observation: the Jacobson closed point inside an intersection of affine opens for (3), the maximal chain inside Z for (7), and the topological supremum over components for (8) (proof lines 3873-3891, 3911-3925).
Derive the monotonicity statements of part (9) and the local ring increment of part (11) from part (7) (proof lines 3928-3934, 3943-3949).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is an eleven-part collection for a locally algebraic k-scheme X: catenarity of the underlying space, dim_x(X) = dim(O_{X,x}) at closed points, invariance of the dimension under nonempty open subsets and at every point when X is irreducible, extendability of chains of irreducible closed subsets to maximal chains of length dim(X), the max-min formula for dim_x(X), dim(X) = trdeg_k(kappa(x)) at the generic point, the drop of the transcendence degree by exactly one along an immediate specialization, dim(X) as the supremum of the transcendence degrees of generic points, the monotonicity of dim_x and dim(O_{X,x}) along specializations together with the length formula for maximal chains, the formula dim_x(X) = trdeg_k(kappa(x)) + dim(O_{X,x}), and the increment of dim(O) by one along an immediate specialization in the irreducible or equidimensional case (statement lines 3782-3845). The author announces that instead of using the more general results proved earlier he will reduce everything to finite type k-algebras and cite the commutative algebra chapter (proof lines 3847-3851). Each part is then routed separately, mostly by replacing X by an affine neighbourhood Spec(A) with A a finite type k-algebra; the steps that are not formal are the reductions themselves, for instance the use of the Jacobson property of X to produce a closed point inside U cap U' in part (3) (proof lines 3876-3883), the use of the rule Z to Z cap U to compare irreducible components pointwise in part (5) (proof lines 3894-3902), and the maximal chain argument in part (7) (proof lines 3911-3918). The claim is H2: no new construction is introduced, but eleven statements each have to be routed to the correct algebra input.
